title: Failed Payment Recovery: How to Stop Revenue Leakage from Failed Payments
description: How to stop revenue leakage from failed payments and recover failed recurring payments — dunning, smart retries, card updater, and DIY vs software.
keywords: how to stop revenue leakage from failed payments

faq.a: Automated retries and customer communication to collect revenue when a subscription charge fails — before the customer churns involuntarily.

faq.q: How to stop revenue leakage from failed payments?
faq.a: Enable smart retries, send branded dunning emails with a one-click payment update link, pre-notify before card expiry, and outreach high-ARPU accounts that still fail.

faq.q: What is failed recurring payment recovery?
faq.a: Failed recurring payment recovery is collecting declined subscription renewals with timed retries, dunning, and card-update links so involuntary churn does not become permanent.

faq.q: How much revenue can dunning recover?
faq.a: Many SaaS businesses recover 20–40% of failed charges with basic retries and emails; strong programs often recover 50–70% of failed dollars.

blocks.text: Failed payment recovery targets involuntary churn — customers who did not intend to leave. Without dunning, you leak MRR that a few emails and retries would save. This brief covers how to stop revenue leakage from failed payments; the full playbook is in the guide linked below.

items: Enable processor Smart Retries (e.g. Stripe Billing)
Send branded dunning emails at day 0, 3, and 7
Link to a hosted update-payment page
Surface failed payments in a weekly ops review
Track recovery rate and revenue recaptured
